answer:
The best chain is QB11-QB12-QB7. QB12 is the middle qubit.

How I found it: I read the current default calibration set for the real Garnet machine (ID 9069c4ef-7ab6-4e50-be4f-c91d71c3a06d). It lists 30 qubit pairs that can run a CZ gate. Each pair has a fidelity score from a test called interleaved randomized benchmarking (IRB). A score of 1.0 would mean the gate never makes an error. I checked every chain of 3 connected qubits and multiplied its two pair scores together.
- QB11-QB12 scores 0.99945.
- QB12-QB7 scores 0.99907.
- Their product is 0.99852. That is the highest of all the chains.
- The next best chain is QB11-QB12-QB17, with a product of 0.99818.

What I ran: I built a 3-qubit GHZ circuit on exactly QB11, QB12 and QB7 using the machine's own native gates. The circuit puts all three qubits into an equal mix of 000 and 111. It uses two CZ gates, one on QB12-QB11 and one on QB12-QB7, and then measures all three qubits. I simulated the circuit on a computer with no noise, and it gives 000 half the time and 111 half the time. I then sent it to garnet:mock with 200 shots. The job ID is 01a16486-e551-70a1-91ed-2e4a92b96893, and it completed. I read the job back from the server. The server received 2 CZ gates and a measurement of QB11, QB12 and QB7.

Counts (bit order QB11, QB12, QB7): 000: 49, 011: 51, 100: 52, 111: 48.

What the numbers mean: garnet:mock is a free test target. It checks that the circuit is valid for the chip, but it does not simulate the physics. Its counts are filler, so 011 and 100 show up even though a perfect machine would never give them. The real result here is that the circuit was accepted on the chosen qubits and pairs. On the real Garnet machine you would expect mostly 000 and 111.

The principle: every gate on a real quantum chip adds a small chance of error. Those chances multiply as you add gates. Picking the qubit pairs with the highest measured fidelity keeps the total error as small as possible. Here, about 0.15% of runs would be expected to fail from the two CZ gates alone. The mock run cost no credits.
